name: Atmosphere
basis: About 90 percent hydrogen and 10 percent helium by volume, with deuterium at 2.6 parts in 100,000 of the hydrogen and helium-3 at under 2 in 10,000 of the helium (Galileo probe); the last two sit at the lowest grade. Known from the Galileo probe.

name: Atmosphere
basis: About 96 percent hydrogen and 3 percent helium by volume in the upper atmosphere (Cassini), helium being depleted against Jupiter; deuterium and helium-3 are traces at the lowest grade. Known from Cassini.

name: Atmosphere
basis: 83 percent hydrogen, 15 percent helium and 2 percent methane by volume, with deuterium at about twice the Jovian share. Known from Voyager 2.

name: Atmosphere
basis: 80 percent hydrogen, 19 percent helium and 1.5 percent methane by volume, with deuterium at about twice the Jovian share. Known from Voyager 2.
